questions.question: When you start an engine, what should happen?

options.text: Warning lights turn on, then turn off quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warning lights turn on, then turn off quickly.
questions.explanation: When a vehicle starts, warning lights should come on for a few seconds, then turn off. If the warning lights stay on, there may be a problem with the vehicle.

questions.question: If there is a fire inside a cargo trailer, what should you do?

options.text: Do not open the trailer doors.
Put a heavy blanket over the trailer.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not open the trailer doors.
questions.explanation: Never open trailer doors during a cargo fire, especially if hazardous materials are inside. Opening the doors gives the fire more oxygen, which makes the fire grow larger.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in fog?
questions.explanation: If you must drive in fog, decrease your speed. This helps you stay safe in poor visibility.

questions.question: What is one way to prevent drowsiness while driving?

options.text: Get enough sleep the night before your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get enough sleep the night before your trip.
questions.explanation: Driving while tired is dangerous. Get a full night's sleep before a long trip. Other ways to prevent drowsiness include having someone ride with you, scheduling trips when you are normally awake, and avoiding medicines that cause drowsiness. Regular exercise can also help you stay alert while driving.

questions.question: How can you secure a second trailer when coupling two trailers together?

options.text: Place it at the base of a hill.

questions.explanation: When coupling a second trailer and you are unsure about the trailer's brakes, use wheel chocks to keep the trailer in place while you couple it.

questions.question: When should you use your turn signal?

options.text: Signal before you begin the turn.
Turn off the signal before you begin the turn.
Signal only if vehicles are in front of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal before you begin the turn.
questions.explanation: Always signal well before you turn. This tells other drivers your plans so they do not try to pass you. Without a signal, drivers may think you are just slowing down, not turning.

questions.question: How can you tell if a converter dolly has anti-lock brakes?

options.text: The dolly has a sticker with the letters "ABS."
There is a plaque on the side of the dolly.
There is a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly.
questions.explanation: Converter dollies made on or after March 1, 1998 must have anti-lock brakes. A yellow lamp on the left side of the dolly shows that anti-lock brakes are present.

questions.question: What is the main cause of death and injury in work zones?
questions.explanation: Speeding is the main cause of injury and death in work zones. Always slow down when driving through a work zone.

questions.question: Which of the following is acceptable during a pre-trip inspection?

options.text: Front tire tread of 3/32 of an inch

questions.explanation: During a pre-trip inspection, check that all tires have enough tread. Front tires need at least 4/32 of an inch of tread in every major groove. Other tires need at least 2/32 of an inch. Do not use tires of different sizes on the same vehicle.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.explanation: Air brakes are a safe and effective way to stop large, heavy vehicles when they are used and maintained properly.

questions.question: What are alcohol evaporators?

options.text: Devices that add alcohol to brake systems to prevent ice from forming.
Only allowed on vehicles carrying hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Devices that add alcohol to brake systems to prevent ice from forming.
questions.explanation: Some air brake systems have an alcohol evaporator. It adds alcohol to the brake system to stop ice from forming, which can damage the brakes.

questions.question: What may rust around wheel nuts mean?
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean the nuts are loose. If you see rust near the wheel nuts, check if they are tight before driving.

questions.question: When can mirror adjustment be checked properly?

options.text: When the vehicle is on a slight incline.

questions.explanation: On a vehicle with one or more trailers, you can only check mirror adjustment accurately when the trailers are straight. Check your mirrors before every trip.

questions.question: Before trying to put out an engine fire, what should you do?

options.text: Press the accelerator to use up the remaining fuel.

questions.explanation: If your engine catches fire, turn it off as soon as you safely can. Do not open the hood when trying to put out the fire.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop if your brakes fail while driving downhill?

options.text: Let the vehicle slow down on its own.
Let rumble strips slow your vehicle.

questions.explanation: If your brakes fail going downhill, find something outside to stop your vehicle. An escape ramp is the best choice. If no escape ramp is available, drive into an open field or side road that is flat or goes uphill.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Talk on your cell phone while driving.
Plan realistic travel time for your trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan realistic travel time for your trip.
questions.explanation: Plan ahead to allow time for traffic delays. This prevents frustration that can lead to aggressive driving. Other ways to prevent aggressive driving include driving at a safe speed, keeping a safe distance from other vehicles, not making gestures at other drivers, and keeping both hands on the steering wheel.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Rely only on warning signals to know if a train is coming.
Rely only on what other motorists do to know if a train is coming.
Do not rely only on warning signals to know if a train is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not rely only on warning signals to know if a train is coming.
questions.explanation: Do not trust only warning signals, gates, or flaggers to alert you to a train. Be extra alert at crossings without gates or signals. At any railroad crossing, assume a train is coming.

questions.question: How should you apply the brake pedal when stopping?
questions.explanation: Push the brake pedal down slowly when stopping. Gradual braking helps you stay in control of your vehicle.

questions.question: Which is not a reason to use your mirrors?

options.text: You are looking at fuel prices.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are looking at fuel prices.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. It is especially important to check mirrors when turning, changing lanes, merging, and doing tight maneuvers.

questions.question: What may rust around wheel nuts mean?
questions.explanation: Rust around wheel nuts may mean they are loose. Check if the nuts are tight when you see rust in that area.
